paragraphs: Here's what I love about this one, friend. Three kings ran out of water in the desert, and the king of Israel decided the LORD had brought them there to lose (2 Kings 3:10). But Jehoshaphat asked a better question: "Is there no prophet of the LORD here?" (2 Kings 3:11). When you're stuck dry in the middle of nowhere, the first move is to ask what the LORD says, not to panic and write the ending yourself.

Then look at the answer. The LORD says, "Dig this valley full of ditches," and also, "You will not see wind or rain, but the valley will be filled with water" (2 Kings 3:16-17). No clouds, no warning, just ditches to dig and a promise to trust. The LORD called it "a simple matter" (2 Kings 3:18), and the next morning the water came, right at the time of the morning sacrifice (2 Kings 3:20). What looks impossible to us is simple for Him, and that is a LOT of room to breathe, baker.

Now notice what kind of help it was. The water that saved the kings was the same water that looked like blood to the Moabites (2 Kings 3:22), and the LORD handed the victory over just as He said. Even then, the story ends on a heavy note that I won't try to make light, because Scripture doesn't hide that some things in this world are dark (2 Kings 3:27). So here's the big idea: when you're dry and out of ideas, ask for the LORD's word, do the plain thing He says, and trust Him for what you can't see yet.
